clips.h3_prompt:
Subject: Landscape 16:9, one continuous 10-second single-character narrative. Show exactly one physical instance of the established heavy adult adventurer from Picture 1. Preserve his broad heavy body, grounded weight, short dark hair, thick dark beard, tired experienced face, layered worn dark clothing, red scarf, crossing straps and buckles, pale metal shoulder and chest structure, complete backpack and rolled equipment, one cyan-lit waist lantern, heavy gloves and boots. Keep every connected item, body proportion, material and reference color unchanged.

Movement: From 0 to 2 seconds he is already standing in a valid stable position, both boots planted, his complete load and all hanging equipment fully settled. From 2 to 4 seconds one ordinary nonverbal mechanical cycle cue occurs from the side supported by Picture 2; there is no danger, alarm or forced movement, and no new mechanism appears. From 4 to 5.5 seconds only the nearest shoulder and attached equipment make one restrained local response while his feet remain planted, showing that the available side clearance is adequate but tight. From 5.5 to 7 seconds his eyes and head turn only slightly to check the lateral space beside his load. From 7 to 9 seconds, without stepping backward or surrendering any forward progress, he deliberately shifts sideways by roughly half the width of one boot into verified open ground. From 9 to 10 seconds he stops immediately; the backpack and hanging equipment settle once, and he remains calm and stable without further correction.

Scene: Picture 2 defines SCENE-05, the same monochrome mechanical-airport environment, its existing technical atmosphere, visible structures, spatial continuity, safe standing area, negative space and original palette logic. Use a nearby environmental cycle only if an existing moving boundary or equivalent element is visibly supported by the bound scene image. Use the lateral open ground only after Work verifies it. Do not invent a door, control panel, display, sign, rail, platform, warning light, extra machine or alternate route.

Camera: One locked eye-level full-body medium-wide three-quarter view in a 16:9 landscape frame. Keep both boots, backpack width, hanging equipment, the verified side clearance and stable ground readable together. Fixed framing, focal length and horizon; no push, pull, pan, tilt, tracking, reframing, cut, transition or split screen. The uncut view must prove that he was already correctly settled before the single lateral adjustment.

Lighting: Preserve the bound character materials and Picture 2's monochrome palette logic. Use one fixed soft diffuse light throughout. Keep the cyan lantern as one small identity light only. No new glow, flashing, relighting, weather change, sudden saturation shift or color redesign.

Atmosphere: He should first read as competent and correctly positioned; the tiny voluntary side shift may then read as experienced consideration rather than indecision or retreat. His appeal comes from giving the surrounding space a little more margin without abandoning his completed progress. Express this through weight, timing and one precise lateral transfer. Use clear two-dimensional hand-drawn shapes, restrained variable-width linework, soft diffuse depth and low-saturation shadows only where compatible with the bound references.

Audio: Ambient soundscape: low mechanical-airport room tone, restrained ventilation, one ordinary non-alarm cycle cue, slight equipment creak, one lateral boot contact and a single backpack-settling sound. Emotional sound cue: one sparse low sustained tone remains quiet during the clearance check and resolves softly when the new stance settles, with no lyrics and no strong beat. Audio supports spatial margin, weight transfer and restrained emotion only; it does not drive cuts and is not music-video editing.

Negative: exactly one character and one physical body, no duplicate character, no second human figure, no split screen, no clone or mirror-double, no reflection person, no crowd, no NPC, no extra limbs, no text overlay, no watermark, no abrupt redesign, no young slim redesign, no removed backpack, no dropped equipment, no duplicate lantern, no new strap, no new buckle, no new weapon, no backward step, no forward passage, no repeated shuffling, no panic, no run, no jump, no acrobatics, no invented mechanism or structure, no camera movement, no cut, no transition, no weather change, no abrupt color shift, no text overlay, no lyrics, no strong beat, no MV editing, no glossy 3D rendering.
